clue.text: The car of your dreams?

parts.note: a railway carriage fitted with bunks is where passengers sleep, and so dream, overnight

explanation.surface: An advert-style question about the motor you have always longed for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Car of your dreams' suggests a fantasy automobile; the car is a railway carriage, and the dreams are literal, had while asleep on an overnight train.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carriage with berths for overnight travellers is called by this name, since passengers spend the night asleep in it.

clue.text: Thus PM defends his specious argument

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: the abbreviation surrounds the word his, as a guard encircles what it defends

explanation.surface: So the Prime Minister stands up for his own dubious reasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: A plausible but fallacious line of reasoning, the kind ancient Sophists were accused of using.

clue.text: Bird with taste for fish, Ruth wants no starter

indicators.note: the synonym lacks its opening letter, the starter of a word

parts.note: ruth is an archaic word for pity or regret

explanation.surface: A woman called Ruth skips the first course when ordering fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' looks like a name; it is the old word for sorrow (as in ruthless), giving REGRET, which loses its first R.
explanation.definitionFit: This white heron wades in shallows and feeds largely on fish.

clue.text: Creature devouring rook and crustacean

indicators.note: the creature swallows the rook letter, taking it inside

parts.note: a creature in the sense of someone's tool or puppet is a pawn
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: An animal eating a bird and a shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: A creature here is a person used by another, a pawn; rook and pawn add a chess undertone.
explanation.definitionFit: This small shellfish with ten legs belongs to the class of crustaceans.

clue.text: Clobber river people invading small island

indicators.note: the people go into the island, placed inside it

parts.note: an ait is a small island in a river, especially the Thames
men means people

explanation.surface: River-borne invaders attack a tiny island and beat it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' looks like a verb (hit) but is British slang for clothes or gear.
explanation.definitionFit: An old literary word for clothing, matching the slang noun for one's clothes.

clue.text: Approachable female appears in a moral tale

indicators.note: the female letter shows up within the phrase a fable, so it is placed inside it

parts.note: a fable is a short story with a moral

explanation.surface: A friendly woman turns up as a character in an improving story.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone affable is friendly and easy to talk to, which is what approachable describes.

clue.text: Adult with young man dressed at last in rubber?

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult
a lad is a young man

indicators.note: the final letter of the word dressed is taken

explanation.surface: A grown-up and a youth finally clad in latex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubber' suggests latex; it is one who rubs, the pantomime hero who rubs the magic lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk-tale hero summons a genie by rubbing his lamp, so he is literally one who rubs.

clue.text: The last word in unchanging time and space

indicators.note: the final word of a prayer goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: firm means fixed or unchanging
amen is the last word of a prayer

explanation.surface: A philosophical-sounding phrase about the ultimate word in eternity and space.
explanation.definitionFit: The firmament is the vault of the heavens, the sky or outer space above.

clue.text: New arrival with £1,000 for instrument

parts.note: a newborn baby is a new arrival
a grand is slang for a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Parents get a newborn and a thousand pounds to buy an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A small version of the horizontal piano is a kind of musical instrument.

clue.text: Message left in eastern skiing area

indicators.note: the letter for left goes inside the ski run

parts.note: a piste is a prepared ski run

explanation.surface: A note was left at an eastern ski resort.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a letter, formal or biblical, a written communication.

clue.text: Parking arranged at a price for each person

parts.note: P is the map and road-sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: the letters are set out in a new order, as things are arranged

explanation.surface: A car park charge has been fixed at a set rate per head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles P with ATAPRICE into the Latin phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase literally means 'by heads', used for amounts reckoned per individual.

clue.text: Leader in congregation cut chat short

indicators.note: short then trims the last letter from what is left, so the word stops before its end
the word for chat is cut back, losing the short particle that ends the phrasal verb

parts.note: to rabbit on is British slang for chattering at length

explanation.surface: A church leader brusquely ends some small talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut ... short' reads as one phrase around 'chat'; the parse splits it, cut removing ON and short the T. To 'rabbit on' (talk endlessly) is British slang, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish religious teacher leads the worshippers of a synagogue, its congregation.

clue.text: Strained decimal point

parts.note: decimal counting is done in tens, hence 'in tens'
E (east) is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A tense decimal point, as if a maths symbol could be anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decimal point' reads as one phrase, but it splits: decimal gives IN TENS and point gives E, a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A strained atmosphere is a tense, highly charged one, an intense mood.

clue.text: Plan announced for man on board

indicators.note: a word announced is spoken out, so the synonym's sound is what counts here

parts.note: a draft is a preliminary plan or sketch

explanation.surface: A scheme is made public for a sailor joining the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' suggests a sailor; it is a piece in the board game draughts (British name for checkers).
explanation.definitionFit: Each playing piece in the British game of checkers is called by this name, a man on the board.

clue.text: Guy Busby-Brown making this cocktail?

parts.note: a guy is a man
a busby is a tall fur hat worn by some soldiers
tan is a shade of brown

explanation.surface: Someone with a double-barrelled name, Guy Busby-Brown, is mixing a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The name looks like a person; it splits into three pieces. A busby is the tall fur hat of British ceremonial regiments.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic mixed drink of whiskey, sweet vermouth and bitters named after the New York borough.

clue.text: Architect horrible about large country home

parts.note: John Nash was the Regency architect of Regent Street and Brighton Pavilion

indicators.note: the word for horrible goes around the letter for large

parts.note: vile means horrible
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An architect hates a large house in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country home' suggests a rural mansion; it is the home of country music, the Tennessee city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tennessee city is the centre of the country music industry, its spiritual home.

clue.text: Free cod ends after sailor vanished

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the sailor

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: letters set free are released to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A fisherman frees the tail ends of the cod after a sailor's catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like a verb with the cod as object; it is the anagram signal, and 'after' puts the sailor first.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who absconded ran off secretly and so disappeared from view.

clue.text: Notice being shut in day before escape

indicators.note: the notice is enclosed by the day before, as if shut inside it

parts.note: the eve is the day before an event
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A prisoner is notified of confinement the day before a breakout.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to avoid or get away from something, a verb synonym of escape.

clue.text: Seconds brought in Waller perhaps doesn't eat

indicators.note: the abbreviation for seconds is taken into the name, placed inside it

parts.note: Fats Waller was the American jazz pianist; 'perhaps' marks him as one example of the name

explanation.surface: A jazz pianist who turns down second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: Fats Waller, the jazz pianist, supplies FATS; the irony of a man nicknamed Fats skipping meals is the surface joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstains from food for a while is going without eating.

clue.text: Hide debts, making one angry

parts.note: an animal's hide is its fur
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: Concealing what you owe enrages someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb, conceal; it is a noun, an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Being furious is being extremely angry, a stronger synonym.

clue.text: Corporation accepting revised date after some delay

indicators.note: the corporation takes in the revised letters, holding them inside

parts.note: corporation is old humorous slang for a large belly

indicators.note: the letters are revised into a new order

explanation.surface: A company agrees to a rescheduled date after hold-ups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company but is jocular old slang for a paunch; 'revised' scrambles the date to ATED and 'accepting' holds it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something late, beyond the expected time, is the adverb's sense.

clue.text: Maybe second-rate celebrity in bubble?

definitions.meaning: a B-list star, a minor famous person, one example of the second rank
a raised swelling of skin or paint, filled with fluid or air

explanation.surface: A minor star living in a protective bubble.
explanation.definitionFit: A swelling on skin or a painted surface is a pocket of fluid or air, like a bubble.

clue.text: Bowling succeeded, breaking two stumps!

indicators.note: the letter breaks into the pair of words, splitting them apart

parts.note: stumps is slang for legs, and leg and pin are both words for a leg
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler shatters two sets of stumps.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the stumps are the wooden posts a bowler aims at; here 'stumps' means legs, giving LEG and PIN (slang for leg).
explanation.definitionFit: Leg spin is a style of cricket bowling where the wrist spins the ball from leg to off.

clue.text: Get drunk with zany banker?

indicators.note: a drunk person is muddled, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: An eccentric financier goes out and gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' suggests a financier; it is a river, something with banks. 'drunk' rearranges GET ZANY.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Chinese river has banks, so whimsically it is a 'banker'.

clue.text: Rat's head Olivia cooked for food parcels

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter
cooked suggests the letters are worked over into something new

explanation.surface: Olivia prepares a rat's head as a meal, a grisly kitchen scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat's head' supplies just the first letter; 'cooked' scrambles the name Olivia.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian pasta squares filled with meat or cheese are little parcels of food.

clue.text: Good to follow advice and shine

parts.note: to listen is to heed advice given

explanation.surface: It pays to take advice and so excel.
explanation.definitionFit: To glisten is to sparkle with reflected light, as wet surfaces do.

clue.text: Awkward person originally held in one trap

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the letter is kept inside the other pieces, as if held captive

parts.note: a net is a trap

indicators.note: the original letter of a word is its first

explanation.surface: Somebody is caught in a snare, an awkward spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy or lacking skill, as does awkward.

clue.text: Pulse in broth that needs stir

indicators.note: a soup that needs stirring will be churned, the letters mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook's note: the pulses in the soup want stirring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like a bean or lentil, at home in broth; it is a heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong regular beat, like a pulse.

clue.text: Social need at regular intervals to get sloshed

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every second one, starting from the second

explanation.surface: Getting drunk is the social need at regular gatherings.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiled is slang for drunk, as is sloshed.

clue.text: SPECTRE to supply such documents as Bond may see?

definitions.text: such documents as Bond may see?

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, flexibly, it signals the letters bending into a new order

explanation.surface: The villainous organisation SPECTRE is feeding James Bond classified papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a verb but is the adverb from supple, signalling SPECTRE plus TO rearranged. SPECTRE is Bond's enemy organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified papers of the highest restriction are what the fictional spy handles.

clue.text: Remote southern mortgage company?

parts.note: a lender is a company providing mortgages

explanation.surface: A mortgage firm in the south seems far away.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender chance is a slim, remote one; both describe little likelihood.

clue.text: Renowned as impotent?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, ..., lacking the power to do something

explanation.surface: Someone famous is described as lacking power.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word into NOT ABLE, the question mark flagging the wordplay reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Worthy of attention and well known, the adjective is a synonym of famous.
